questions.q: In the lesson's demonstration, monthly spend was sent to the model in cents instead of dollars. What happened?
options: It ran without any error, predicted about 95% churn on average, and accuracy fell to 0.260
The pipeline raised an error and refused to predict
Accuracy stayed the same because scaling cancels out unit changes
The model automatically converted the units back to dollars
questions.explain: The model returned valid-looking probabilities for every row with no warning, but its predictions were badly wrong. That is a silent failure.

questions.q: Which failure is usually the most dangerous, and why?
options: Loud failures, because they stop the whole service
None of them, because a good test score prevents all of them
Loud failures, because they always corrupt the saved model file
Silent failures, because nothing crashes and nobody is alerted while predictions are wrong
questions.explain: A crash gets noticed and fixed. Silent and slow failures keep producing plausible output, so the cost accumulates unseen.

options: The data the model receives in production differs from the data it was trained on
The training set is larger than the test set
The model trains more slowly than it serves predictions
The model file is saved with a different extension than it is loaded with
questions.explain: Skew is a mismatch between training-time and serving-time inputs, such as different units, columns or feature definitions.

questions.q: Two extra support calls per customer raised the average predicted churn from 0.234 to 0.399, while accuracy only dropped to 0.728. What does this illustrate?
options: A bug in scikit-learn's predict_proba method
Drift: the input population shifted, and the model's behavior changed even though no code broke
That accuracy is always the best monitoring metric
That the model was overfitting the training set
questions.explain: Drift means real-world data moves away from the training data. Watching only accuracy would understate how much the model's outputs changed.

questions.q: Which set best describes what a notebook hides that production needs?
options: Charts, markdown and code comments
The learning rate and the number of trees
Data version, execution order, environment versions and ownership
The name of the target column
questions.explain: The lesson lists four hidden things: which data and version, which cells ran in what order, which library versions, and who owns the model after launch.
